Commentary.Commentary: Right then! It all started with Sarfraz Ahmed, then went to Azhar Ali and now Misbah-ul-Haq, Pakistan have been ruthless on this tour as they have stamped their authority in all the three formats. Pakistan management will be the happiest today to say the least. On the other hand, it has been a tough tour for the West Indies as they are still searching for a win. Well, they have a last chance to do so as the third and final Test will be played at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium starting from 30th October, 2016 at 1130 IST. Will Pakistan manage another whitewash? Join us then to find out. Until next time, it's goodbye from us. Cheerio!

Pakistan skipper MISBAH-UL-HAQ begins by thanking the Almighty. Adds that it wasn't easy to take 20 wickets on this wicket and credits the bowlers for raising to the expectations. Calls it a collective performance from the pacers and especially Yasir Shah to step up. Acknowledges that they know how to utilize their resources. Mentions that it is important to learn and improve every day. (On changing the way Pakistan play) Confesses that he does look to get used to the conditions well and then execute their plans. Adds that UAE is too slow and hence grinding the opposition becomes more important. (On going to New Zealand, Australia) He adds that he is looking forward to the tours and Pakistan will have to tweak their game a bit. Credits his bowlers for working hard on such tracks in UAE and hopes that they continue to get better.

West Indies skipper, JASON HOLDER says that they are happy to have taken the games deep (into Day 5) but need to start Tests better. Acknowledges that they did not bat well in the first innings. Adds that they are pleased to see some application from the batsmen. Credits Blackwood for mixing caution with aggression and also mentions that it was good to see Hope fighting it out. Mentions that they have let themselves down with the drops, if they drop chances, good batsmen will make them pay. Credits his team for coming back well on the second day but hopes they can capitalize on crucial moments ahead. Calls Pakistan a very good Test side and ends by saying that West Indies have not been consistent enough.

Man of the Match, YASIR SHAH begins by thanking Almighty for helping him bowl in the right areas consistently. Confesses the wickets in UAE are conducive to his bowling and hence the expectations too are also high. Admits that he did bowl bad balls but worked hard in the nets to get better. Adds that he plans for each and every series and thanks his seniors in Younis, Misbah and bowling coach Mushtaq for helping him along to get better.

On this deck, you got to give credit to the pacers who did bowl their hearts out and in the end it was overall a collective effort from Pakistan. Not to forget that mammoth stand of 175 runs between Younis Khan and Misbah-ul-Haq in the first innings that ultimately set the tone for the hosts. Note for the stat lovers - This is also Pakistan's 10-match winning streak across all formats, a huge achievement in itself. Let's see what the skippers have to say as the presentation is not that far away...

Chasing a stiff target of 456, West Indies did start off well but most of their batsmen threw it away and made the task all the more difficult for themselves. The opener Kraigg Brathwaite and Jermaine Blackwood applied themselves on this track but couldn't last long. The latter played a classical innings only to be dismissed on 95 today. The tail in the name of Bishoo and Hope then weaved around for a bit but they were just delaying the inevitable.

The veteran Younis Khan uproots one of the stumps and is running around. Yasir Shah is leading his team to the dressing room and is tossing the cherry proudly. What a moment this is for them! Pakistan have emerged victorious yet again and have sealed the series 2-0. It's almost impossible to beat them in UAE, isn't it? West Indies put in their all but the fight wasn't that convincing one as of the Day/Night Test. Yasir Shah spun the web around the Caribbeans and topped the bowling chart with his fabulous figures, picking up his 2nd 10-wicket haul in the white attire.

OUT! GAME. SET. MATCH AND SERIES TO PAKISTAN! Floated outside off, Bishoo looks to slog sweep but top edges it. Sarfraz screams 'Misbah Bhai' as soon as the ball went up in the air. Misbah runs across from short mid-wicket and takes the catch to complete a clinical victory. PAKISTAN WIN BY 133 RUNS!

Plunges forward and defends it solidly back to Yasiraaa.

Welcome back! SHAI HOPE and DEVENDRA BISHOO are out to bat. PAKISTAN begin the session with YASIR SHAH. Here we go...
...DAY 5...SESSION 2...

The visitors still need 184 more runs to win and will know they will have to bat out of their skins to save this game, let alone winning it from here. Pakistan are all over them right now and needing three wickets, they will want to wrap this up quickly. Do join us in a bit for the second session of the day.

West Indies have again been Yasir'ed here! Three wickets in the session and all of them to Yasir. Pakistan struck early to get rid of Chase as he was nicely caught at slips. Yasir then came back to dismiss Blackwood who fell just five short of a valiant ton. The runs were flowing with the new ball for the Windies. Holder tried to hit out as well but was dismissed lbw giving Yasir his fifth wicket, eighth five-wicket haul in Tests.

8th five-wicket haul for Yasir Shah in Tests!

Pushes it towards point for nothing.

Nevertheless, a fighting innings comes to an end and Pakistan just 4 wickets away from winning this Test.

YASIR SHAH to bowl from the other end.

FOUR! Poor effort, Sohail! On a length on off, comes in, Blackwood just leans across and clips it towards mid on. The fielder dives over it and allows it through long on for a boundary. Good start for West Indies! 50-run stand up between Blackwood and Chase!
Fuller outside off, Blackwood drives it hard through covers but not in the gap.
Edged! On a fuller length again, Blackwood looks to defend but gets an outside edge towards covers.
Full again outside off, Blackwood just presses forward and pushes it to covers. The shot was almost like a second thought. This is how he had got out in the first innings, chasing a wide one.
Fuller outside off, Blackwood pushes it towards covers off his crease.
On  a length outside off, defended back down the wicket.

Time for action! 90 overs, 285 runs needed for the visitors, the hosts need 6 more wickets to win - Here we go! The players are out in the middle. JERMAINE BLACKWOOD and ROSTON CHASE to bat now for West Indies. Pakistan begin with RAHAT ALI!

PITCH REPORT - Bazid Khan reckons that the pitch is still bound well thanks to the sand that flows across the desert as per the curator. He mentions that there are some cracks for the spinners to make use of. Adds that it will be a slower wicket, pacers will have to work harder.

Recently, West Indies were in a similar position at Sabina Park at home against India. They were taken to safety by Roston Chase who scored a brilliant ton. The visitors will want him to emulate that performance and see them through. The spinners have got assistance from the pitch and Yasir Shah and Zulfiqar Babar will be more than handful here. Let's see how they go today.

Hello everyone and welcome to the coverage of the final day of the penultimate Test between Pakistan and West Indies from Sheikh Zayed Stadium, Abu Dhabi. Pakistan need six wickets to win the game and seal the series 2-0, West Indies have a tall order in front of them - needing 285 runs to try and stay in the series with an unlikely win.
...DAY 5....SESSION 1...

That is it from us then! Will the Windies be able to fight hard again and come out on the right side of the line this time? Or will Pakistan seal the series here itself? Join us at 1130 IST (0600 GMT) tomorrow for all the action from the fifth and final day of this Test match. Until then, Adios! Take Care!

Pakistan have had to toil hard. Bazid Khan said in his pitch report this morning that the cracks have widened a lot and plenty of turn could be expected but nothing of that sort happened. There was some spin but nothing alarming and most of the wickets were gifted. The hosts though, would be aware of how hard they had to bowl to win the first Test and will aim to break this partnership first thing in the morning and then go through the lower middle order.

Kraigg Brathwaite held one end up with a patient 67 but the others have not quite converted their starts. Johnson departed early but Bravo and Samuels were dismissed after getting set in their innings. They had decent partnerships all the way through, except during the time when Samuels and Brathwaite fell in quick succession but Blackwood and Chase have put some confidence back in the dressing room with an unbeaten 47-run stand. They will hope to dig in tomorrow morning and try and keep Pakistan at bay.

Not a bad day for West Indies, to be honest. Yes, they are facing an uphill task while trying to chase down 456 for an improbable win but they have not thrown it away. 86/2 in the second session and 85/2 in the last one show the manner and calmness with which they have played.

We are set for a fascinating final day of cricket again. West Indies need 285 runs and Pakistan require 6 wickets, with minimum of 90 overs scheduled for tomorrow. However, the issue for the visitors is that they have maybe only one recognized batsman to come, in Shai Hope.
Short and outside off, punched towards mid off for a lately decided single. STUMPS ON DAY 4!
Full and flat, around off, probably the straighter one, defended watchfully.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Outside off, left alone.
Short and outside off, dragged towards deep mid-wicket.

MISCUE! Strange cricket from Blackwood. It is the final over of the day and he decides to go over the top. The ball spins away from outside leg and he miscues this over extra cover and luckily for him, it lands safely. Two runs taken.
We are down to the final over of the day...
The batsman works it down the leg side.
A short ball on middle and off, Blackwood fends it down behind square leg for a single.
Stays back in his crease and punches it away.
On a good length outside off, coming in, punched back to the bowler.
Full and straight, pushed back to Sohail.

NOT OUT. Waste of a review. Plenty of reverse swing, coming in from well outside off, Blackwood missed his flick and got hit on the pads but you could see two stumps when the ball hit the pads. To the naked eye itself, it seemed like missing the leg stump and Hawk Eye showed it to miss, after Pakistan took a review to challenge the umpire's decision on the LBW appeal.
Review time! Pakistan reckon they have Blackwood in front here. The umpire does not agree and they have taken the review. Will they strike in the dying moments of the day?

We are into overtime but just 2 overs left. The over rate has been excellent. Interesting to see, Shai Hope is padded up while Devendra Bishoo is chilling out with his other mates. One would have thought a nightwatchman would have been padded up.
FOUR! A short ball on middle, Chase goes back and whips it aerially over mid-wicket for a boundary! 289 more to win now. The stand moves to 43.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
That is a beauty. Tossed up outside off, draws the batsman forward to defend and then gets it to spin away.
Full and around off, pushed back to the bowler.
Landed outside off, spinning away, left alone.
The batsman has been struck on the thigh pad. The umpire signals a leg bye.

Sohail Khan is covering the ball with his right hand before delivering. He is trying not to show the batsman which side is the shiny side. Waqar Younis on air says that Wasim Akram used to do this a lot and adds that Aaqib Javed tried to emulate him but flopped big time.
That ball has taken the inside edge of the batsman and thudded into his pads.
Close to a yorker, very full outside off, pushed back to the bowler.
An excellent yorker on middle, Chase digs it out.
Punches it towards mid on and takes a quick single. Rahat Ali was caught on his heels there.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off, stays low a touch, Chase looks to push inside the line and is beaten.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Pushed to the cover region by the batsman. They pick up a single.

OUCH! That would have hurt. A full toss on middle, Blackwood flicks it through square leg and the ball hits Azhar Ali at short leg on his right boot and then deflects to short mid-wicket. Azhar is down but gets up in a while.
Short and outside off, Blackwood backs away and punches it but finds cover.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and outside off, driven towards mid off.
Full and outside off, pushed towards mid on.
That came back in a long way from outside off, some reverse swing on offer. Jermaine somehow manages to work it to the leg side for a single.
A short ball outside off, Blackwood sways away from the line.
SOHAIL KHAN returns. Waqar Younis feels that the effort put in by Sohail Khan in the previous over to try and save the boundary would have helped him as he would have warmed up.
Quicker and flatter outside off, Chase looks to cut but misses.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully.

CLOSE! FOUR! Full on leg stump, Chase pushes this uppishly and it just goes wide of Yasir, to his left. The ball races down the ground. Zulfiqar Babar from mid on and Sohail Khan from mid off chase after it and the latter slides to stop the ball but cannot do so.
On middle and leg, defended towards square leg.
Short ball on middle, Chase goes back and punches it towards short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, pushed straight to cover.
Full and outside off, defended from the crease.
Around middle, angling down, turned behind square leg for a well-run couple. The stand moves to 31 now.
Beaten! A rash shot from Blackwood. A length ball outside off, cutting back in, Blackwood looks to punch it through the off side but is beaten.
Landed outside off, punched towards cover.
That is a wild delivery. Full and miles outside off, left alone. Lucky not to be signalled a wide.
Pushes this towards mid on.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
The batsman works it down the leg side. They manage to come back for the second.
Outside leg, Blackwood goes at this with soft hands, half-heartedly and gets an inside edge which goes wide of short leg. A run taken.
Full on middle and leg, Roston comes forward and pushes it towards mid off for a single. 150 UP FOR WEST INDIES.
Tossed up outside leg, Chase keeps it out towards short mid-wicket.
Full and outside off, pushed towards point.
Back of a length on middle, Chase hops and works it through mid-wicket for a run.
On middle and leg, tucked through mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and off, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, well defended this time.

FOUR! Lovely shot. A length ball outside off, Blackwood cuts it past the fielder diving at point and gets a boundary! Moves to 30 from just 34 balls. This stand is worth 23. 309 more needed for a win now.
Full and around middle, jammed towards short extra cover.
Short again, punched towards cover.
Short and outside off, punched towards point.
Full and outside off, defended watchfully towards cover.
Well bowled. Tossed up outside leg, gets a bit of drift, Chase looks to flick but is undone by the drift and gets a leading edge which nearly carries to the bowler!
Tossed up on middle and leg, worked to the leg side for a single.
Landed around off, going away, stays down, Roston jumps and defends.

Full on middle, punched towards Rahat again who tries to stop it but gets fingertips to the ball. It goes through and tests Zulfiqar Babar at mid on who hobbles after it. Misbah gets to it quicker from mid off. The batsmen take a couple.
Goes for the yorker but gets it full outside off, Chase pushes it back to the bowler.
Good single. Pitched on middle and off, JB pushes it towards mid on, sees that it is Zulfiqar Babar over there and takes him on. Completes the single quite easily.
Full and just outside off, Jermaine keeps it out.
A loosener, full and miles outside off, swinging away, Blackwood lets it go.
RAHAT ALI comes back on to bowl.
Fullish in length, attacking the stumps here, Yasir Shah. Roston Chase stands his ground and blocks it out with a straight bat.
On a slightly flatter trajectory, Roston with an expansive drive to the covers. Unfortunately, it's straight to the fielder there.
Shah gives this plenty of revs and tosses it on the stumps, Chase waits for it and then works it to mid-wicket for nothing.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Floated delivery well outside off, it's pushed to the cover region. Won't get any run for it.
Floated on middle and off, Chase leans forward and meets it with a straight blade.
Full and attacking the stumps, it's bowled slower through the air, Jermaine Blackwood pushes it back to Nawaz to end the over.
Drags the length back on this and pitches it around off, no trouble for JB to go back and play it to point.
Flighted from Mohammad Nawaz, drifting in on middle and leg, Jermaine Blackwood dances down the wicket and plays it back to the bowler.
Solid from Jermaine. Leans forward and dead-bats this full ball into the track ahead.
Drifting in on middle and leg, Chase eases it down to mid on and takes a quick run.
Fuller in length outside off, driven through to long off for one run.
Yasir gives this plenty of air and tosses it up around off, Chase comes forward and blocks.
Flighted ball on the stumps, it's kept out off the front foot.
Pierced the gap well here. Blackwood backs away, makes room and places it through the covers well. Made good use of the wrists too and as a result, was able to run three.
Shorter in length and outside off, punched away. Dot ball.
Jermaine Blackwood presents a solid front foot defense to keep this full ball out.
Looped up well by Yasir Shah, Blackwood leans ahead and with a closed face, works it through mid-wicket for a brace.
Lovely variation from the left-armer, tosses it up and gets plenty of drift on this, Roston Chase presses forward and blocks it out.
Shortens the length on this and keeps it around off, Roston punches it on the off side for nothing.
Fullish in length pitched outside off once more, Chase pushes it to covers.
Arm ball drifting in from around off, Roston Chase keeps it out from deep within his crease.
Low full toss on middle and leg, it's drilled back down the track. Nawaz does well to run to his right and stop the ball from going past him.
Floats it up from outside off, it's driven to covers for a single.
Shorter and flatter outside off, a back foot punch to end the over.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single.
BEAUTY FROM YASIR! Tosses up a wonderful leg breaker around off, it goes past JB's outside edge and into Sarfraz's gloves. So close. Could have easily taken the edge there.
Short and wide outside off, Jermaine stays back and slaps it hard straight to the man at covers.

FOUR! Tossed up around off, Jermaine Blackwood steps out to this one and lofts it hard over wide mid on. Clears the infield with ease as the ball races away to the fence. The leggie isn't sad about that one bit, he's liking this challenge.
Straighter one on the leg stump line, Blackwood looks to flick it across the line but misses as the ball goes off his pads. Muted appeal for a leg before but the umpire doesn't show any interest.
Arm ball which comes in with the angle, on the pads, it's clipped down towards fine leg for a couple.
Darted on off stump, Chase just about manages to bring his bat down to this one. That came in quite quicker than he probably anticipated.
ROSTON CHASE walks in at number 6, replacing Brathwaite.

OUT! NAWAZ GETS HIS MAN! And that's of the set Kraigg Brathwaite. Pakistan have a big reason to smile here. Nawaz bowls an arm ball and it's going on with the angle on middle and leg, Kraigg Brathwaite goes back to defend but misses and is rapped on the pads. There are appeals for an lbw but the umpire shakes his head. The entire Pakistan team is unconvinced and ultimately, decide to take the review. And what a review it is. Replays show the ball to be hitting the leg stump. Brathwaite has to make the long walk back after playing a good knock.
Kraigg Brathwaite is caught leg before and is adjudged not out. Pakistan are not happy with that and decide to take a review against the decision.
Flatter and slightly shorter in length around off, kept out off the back foot.
Flatter and keeping a bit low as well, on middle and leg, Brathwaite does well to bring his bat down in time to defend as he goes back to defend.
Floats it up from around the wicket, outside off, it's pushed to the covers for no run.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

AN ABSOLUTE RIPPER FROM YASIR SHAH! Tossed up leg-spinner on off, it turns away heavily as Blackwood looks to block it off the front foot. Beats the outside edge and goes into the keeper's gloves. Now that's the length he should be bowling.
Loopy leg breaker around off, blocked.
FOUR! Great use of the feet here. Jermaine Blackwood gets to the pitch of the delivery and whacks it over mid on to send it all the way.
Turning away on a shorter length, outside off, punched to covers.
Blackwood has asked for a cap and a change of gloves.
Full on the stumps, defended off the front foot.

Coming in with the angle on middle and leg, Jermaine Blackwood tucks it through backward square leg once more, Younis Khan and Sohail Khan are the men running to get it. The former runs faster here and keeps the batsmen to three runs. Good athleticism shown by the veteran.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
On a good length and coming in from outside off, blocked off the back foot.
Jermaine Blackwood steps out this flighted delivery around off and plays it back to the bowler off the inside half.
Loopy and turning away from around off, it's played to point for no run.

He's run four here. Great running that. Full toss drifting in on middle and off, Blackwood clips it through backward square leg. The fielders are quite late to get to the ball, it is a big outfield in their defense. But this allows the batsmen to run four. Great stuff.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full on middle and leg, Blackwood drives this towards long off and takes a single.

Some serious drift and dip for Yasir Shah. He gives this a lot of air and tosses it up on middle and leg, almost a yorker really. Blackwood clears his front leg and gets it off the outer part on the off side.
JERMAINE BLACKWOOD walks in at number 5, replacing Samuels.

OUT! "YASIRA" STRIKES! He's provided the breakthrough yet again. A rather soft dismissal in hindsight, though. Too full from the leggie, Marlon Samuels drives it straight back to Yasir on the up. He takes it with ease and starts celebrating. The umpire however just wants to check if it's a bump ball or not. So the decision goes upstairs and replays show that it is not. Samuels is gone and that's another wicket down for West Indies.
Samuels is caught and bowled. But the umpire just wants to make sure if it is a bump ball or not. The soft signal is out.
Loopy leg-spinner from Yasir Shah and it's pitched outside off, eased down to long off for a comfortable single.
Loopy and full on middle and off, pushed back in the direction of the bowler.
Full ball on the stumps, it's driven down to long on for one run.
Kraigg Brathwaite gets right behind the line and defends this flatter delivery.

Stifled appeal but that was going down leg. Quicker one pushed through by Nawaz, it's on leg and angling down, raps Kraigg on the pads as he goes back to flick it across the line. Appeal is rightly turned down.
The batsman has flicked the ball off his pads. One run added to the total.
Arm ball from Nawaz, going on with the angle, Marlon goes behind and keeps it out from deep within the crease.
Drifting in from around the wicket, it's kept out well from within the crease.
MOHAMMAD NAWAZ comes on to bowl now.
Full and around off, defended off the inside portion of the bat towards the bowler.
On middle, pushed back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Flatter this time, around off, a bit of spin, defended from the crease again, to the leg side.
That is a beauty. On the mark, pitched around leg, Kraigg plays him on the back foot and misjudges the length. Is squared up as the ball spins away and somehow pushes it to the off side.
Short and wide outside off, Brathwaite reaches out and slaps it but finds cover.
YASIR SHAH is back on.
On middle and leg, tucked through square leg for a brace.
This time he comes forward and defends.
Full and outside off, Marlon plays it away from his body and pushes it back to the bowler off a slightly inner portion of the bat.
Outside off, pushed towards point.
Comes back into the right-hander quite sharply, Kraigg just about manages to tuck it through backward square leg for a single. 349 more needed to win.
FOUR! Nicely played. Short and outside off, Brathwaite does not go too hard it, albeit just places it behind point and finds the gap and the boundary. The stand moves to 43.
Driven through mid off by the batsman. They pick up a single. Moves to 60.
Comes down the track and pushes it down the track to long off for a single. Moves to 20.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Full and around middle, Samuels looks to defend but gets a thick inside edge which just goes wide of short leg.
Deep backward square leg moves to mid-wicket.
Comes forward and works it through mid-wicket for a single. 100 IS UP FOR WEST INDIES!
Full on middle and leg, flicked through mid-wicket.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot. They pick up a single.
Full and outside off, driven back to the bowler.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and outside off, played straight to point.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Full and outside off, driven straight to mid off.
The batsman has been struck on the pads as he looked to play that off the front foot.
Landed outside off, defended watchfully.
Outside off, driven through mid off for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed towards extra cover.
Similar ball, same reaction.
Pitched outside leg, Brathwaite comes forward to defend.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and outside off, this is hit hard towards mid off. Samuels takes a couple of steps for the single but is sent back as Misbah has a shy at his end.

FOUR! UPPISH, BUT WIDE! Full and wide outside off, Samuels reaches out and goes hard with the drive. The ball goes in the air but evades a diving Yasir Shah at backward point and races to the fence. He is looking in an ultra positive mood since Tea. 359 more needed for a win now.
Outside off, played straight to point.
Bouncer! The batsman ducks in time to let that one go over him.
On middle and off, punched towards mid on.
Outside off, punched towards cover.
Another arm ball, around off, Brathwaite defends it in front of his stumps.
Full and wide outside off, KB leans and drives it straight to cover.
Full again, defended by coming forward.
Very full outside off, Kraigg reaches out and pushes it back to the bowler.
Landed around off, angled in, Brathwaite stays back and defends.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full on middle, swinging in, flicked through square leg for a couple. The stand is worth 30 now.
Full and wide outside off, Samuels blasts it through mid off but Misbah gets across quickly to his left and slides to his left to stop.
Outside off, a play and a miss.
Outside off, angling away, left alone.
On a good length outside off, punched through the covers for a single.
RAHAT ALI to bowl from the other end.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
This time he stays in his crease and defends.
FOUR! Nicely done! Flighted on middle, Marlon comes down the track and lofts it over mid-wicket and gets a boundary! Moves to 13. 366 more needed for a win now.
Comes down the track and drives it towards mid on.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Full and down the leg side, Samuels misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
We are back for the final session of the day. It will be Kraigg Brathwaite and Marlon Samuels to continue with Zulfiqar Babar taking the ball first up.
... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

West Indies will be happy with the runs they got. They were positive in their approach but have lost two wickets in the process. They will hope to see off the 31 overs remaining today and then see what happens tomorrow. Brathwaite has been playing superbly while Samuels is trying to get his eye in. Join us back at 1630 IST (1100 GMT) for the final session.

Not a bad session for Pakistan. They know it will be hard work for them to pick up 10 wickets and have nipped out 2. They got them pretty cheaply and did not have to work very hard for it, with both Johnson and Bravo throwing their wickets away.
On a good length just outside off, Kraigg Brathwaite moves towards the ball and taps it down into the track just under his nose. THAT WILL BE TEA ON DAY 4!
Good length ball outside off, blocked off the back foot on the off side.

Too full on off stump, Samuels with the full face of the bat drives it straight back through the bowler's legs. Misbah-ul-Haq chases it down from mid off and keeps it just inside the ropes. Saves the boundary and restricts the batsmen to three.
What are you doing, Marlon Samuels? You're so close to tea, just let it go. It's wide, wide outside the off stump, Samuels still goes after it. He missed it but could have just as easily nicked that.
Sohail Khan brings out the short one and bangs it in hard, Samuels ducks in time and evades it well.
Good length ball on off, defended from within the crease.
The batsman charges down the wicket. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Looped up on the stumps, it's drilled to covers.

Fullish on middle and leg, the ball goes off Samuels' pads as he tries to play it off the front foot. It lobs over as the fielder from short leg comes in to take it. Pakistan appeal for a catch but it's rightly turned down.
Full and flighted on the stumps, it's driven back down the ground. A superb save from Yasir Shah at long off keeps the batsmen down to two.
Drifting in on middle and leg, Samuels is caught on the pads as he comes forward to defend.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Shaping in from around off, Brathwaite closes the face and works it to the mid-wicket region. That's the end of the over.
Fired in full and outside off, Kraigg brings a straight blade down to this one and pushes it to the cover fielder.
Fullish in length and on the stumps, blocked.
Fuller length delivery outside off, pushed to cover-point for no run.
Slightly fuller in length, swinging away from around off, Brathwaite brings his bat down in time and keeps it out.
Good length delivery just around the off stump, Brathwaite stays back and keeps it out.
Full outside off, Marlon drives it to covers.
Turning away from outside off, Samuels is beaten as he tries to play inside the line. Goes past the outside edge and into the keeper's gloves.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
2000 Test runs for Kraigg Brathwaite!
Loopy and full outside off, Kraigg Brathwaite leans forward and across and drives it crisply through the covers. Gets it in the gap nicely and as a result, picks up three runs for it.
Some serious drift on this occasion for Zulfiqar Babar, tosses it up outside off, pushed to the cover region.
Floated well from around the wicket, just outside off, a solid front foot defense presented by KB.
Fullish in length outside off, shaping away, Marlon Samuels taps it away on the off side to end the over.
Outside off, played to point.
That's a very good leave by Marlon Samuels. It's fuller in length and swinging away, outside off, Samuels moves towards the ball and makes a watchful leave.
Fuller in length outside off, blocked.
Fuller length ball going down leg, Samuels goes after it but misses it completely.
Length ball aiming the top of off stump, kept out from deep within the crease.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Turning away from outside off, left alone.
Fuller length ball on the stumps, it's driven to mid on. No run taken.
Another arm ball from Zulfiqar Babar, he keeps it on the shorter side around off, Brathwaite is a little cramped for room as he cuts it away. Only manages to find the fielder.
Kraigg Brathwaite stays back and punches it off the back foot on the off side.
Drifting in from outside off, on a length, Kraigg backs away and cuts it square on the off side.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Angling back in sharply from a length and on middle and off, it's played off the inside half towards mid on.
Coming in sharply from middle and off, on the hips really, it's tucked behind square on the leg side for a couple of good runs.
Shortish delivery outside off, Kraigg drags it towards mid-wicket and once again sets off quickly to complete a single.
On the shorter side once more, Samuels rises on top of the bounce, rolls his wrists and works it towards mid-wicket. One run is taken as the fielder is too deep.
Just back of a length, Samuels waits for the ball to come to him, it doesn't look dangerous at all. Marlon blocks it out rather comfortably.
SOHAIL KHAN is back on.
Pitched on a good length and turning away a bit from outside off, Kraigg has nothing to do with that.
Brathwaite defends this length delivery from within the crease.
Short and wide outside off, cut away straight to backward point.
On the shorter side once more, punched away off the back foot. No run taken.
Similar delivery, this one is closer to the stumps but it's still left alone by Kraigg Brathwaite.
Loopy and turning away from way outside off, left alone for the keeper to collect.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Angling in on a length from outside off, Samuels covers the line perfectly and keeps it out on the off side.
11th Test fifty for Kraigg Brathwaite!

Brilliant knock from KB. Low full toss on off, Kraigg flicks it through the gap in the mid-wicket region. Sohail Khan is the man giving it the chase and it seems like he's running forward. That's a really huge ground. The batsmen end up taking three runs and Brathwaite has completed his fifty with this.
Coming in on middle and leg, it's turned to the on side for nothing.
Fuller length delivery around off, blocked off the front foot.
Length ball angling in from outside off, tapped away on the off side for no run.
Floats it up on middle and leg, eased down to long on for a single. Brathwaite moves on to 48.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on the stump, KB presses forward and presents a straight bat to defend.
FOUR! Kraigg Brathwaite is looking in good knick. Makes good of his feet, gets to the pitch of the ball and slogs it nicely over the mid-wicket region to pick up a boundary.
Similar delivery, Babar gets it to drift in from around off, Kraigg stays behind the line to block.
Floats this one up from outside off, it's drifting in, kept out off the front foot.
Another back foot defense presented to end the over.
On a good length and outside off, Marlon Samuels goes back, opens his body up a bit and taps it away on the off side.
Rahat Ali brings out the short one and pounds it in hard. Samuels does well to duck and evade.
Fullish in length and outside off, blocked.
Rahat Ali has a change of angle and comes from around the wicket, angles in a length ball from outside off, Samuels stays back and keeps it out.
Pitched slightly ahead of a length on middle and leg, it's flicked through the mid-wicket region for one run.
Length delivery outside off, played to point for a single.
Babar nicely floats it up around off, it's coming in with the angle, Brathwaite steps forward and across and plays it back to the bowler off the inside half.
Coming in on a good length, some decent air given to this, the batsman goes back and punches it on the off side.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Some dip on this occasion, drifting in once again, Kraigg Brathwaite gets behind the line and defends it out from deep within his crease.
Drifting in from around the wicket, Kraigg brings his bat down to this and keeps it out.
MARLON SAMUELS jogs to the middle at number 4, replacing Bravo.

OUT! Rahat Ali gets the big fish! Short and wide outside off, some movement in the air on this occasion, Bravo rocks back and cuts it hard. It's in the air and straight into the hands of Mohammad Nawaz at backward point who pouches it with ease. The southpaw has been the one to lead the Windies' charge with the bat. Big, big breakthrough for Pakistan, this.
Good length delivery outside off, Bravo withdraws his bat and watches as the ball goes past him.
Fuller length delivery on middle and leg, a little too straight from the left-armer, Kraigg Brathwaite flicks it through mid-wicket and runs to the other end to complete a single.
Very full and outside off, Kraigg reaches out to this one and firmly drives it straight to the man at covers.
Some reverse swing for Rahat Ali. He fires it in full and on middle and off, going away from the batsman as he blocks it out on the on side.
Length ball just outside off, tight line from Rahat Ali, it's worked in front of covers for a brisk single.

Lovely delivery from Zulfiqar Babar, lands it just back of a driving length and invites Brathwaite forward to drive. The right-hander gets a leading edge a little square on the off side as he looks to drive it through the covers.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Loopy and fullish in length outside off, driven to covers for no run.
Babar bowls this slower through the air and gives it plenty of air, it's drifting in as Kraigg Brathwaite just works it on the on side.
Full and floated on off, pushed in front of covers for nothing.
Comes from around the wicket and drifts it in on middle and off, Kraigg gets perfectly behind the line and keeps it out on the off side.
ZULFIQAR BABAR replaces Yasir Shah.
Once again it's on the shorter side, once again it's punched off the back foot to the covers.
Back of a length delivery just outside off, it's punched off the back foot to short cover.
Another one which is right up there, just outside off, Darren Bravo drives it to the cover region but won't get any run for it.
Fuller ball aiming the base of off stump, Bravo punches it back down the track.
Back of a length delivery on the body, Brathwaite swivels across and pulls it away through backward square leg for a single.

Rahat Ali comes steaming in and fires in a full delivery across the right-hander, Kraigg Brathwaite leans forward and drives it back past the bowler. The fielder from mid off comes across to cut it off and restricts the batsmen from taking a single.
Drinks break!
FOUR! Lovely stroke! Full and loopy on middle and off, Darren Bravo just drives this back past mid off and sends it all the way. Great timing on that shot.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Similar ball from Yasir Shah, defended from within the crease into the track.
Turning in to the left-hander, pitched right up there, it's dropped in front of short leg.
Floats it up nicely outside off, no trouble for Kraigg to just ease it through to wide long off for one.

Yasir tosses it up on middle and off, it's a little too full as Bravo drives it to the left of the leggie, beats him as well as the spinner dives and tries to save it. A single is taken as the ball goes to long on.
A short ball outside leg, Kraigg gets across and lets the ball go.
Full and wide outside off, Darren leans and pushes it through the covers for a run.
Full and outside off, driven uppishly but wide of short extra cover towards mid off.
On middle, Brathwaite gets across and works it through mid-wicket for a single.
On middle and leg, worked towards short mid-wicket.
Full and around off, pushed towards mid off.
RAHAT ALI is back on.
On middle and leg, worked straight to square leg.
On middle, worked straight to short mid-wicket
Flatted around off, defended back to the bowler.
Shorter and flatter around off, punched down to long off for a single.
The batsman has punched the ball off the back foot.
Full on middle, pushed down to long on for a single.
The batsman rocks onto the back foot and punches the ball. One run added to the total. 50 UP FOR WEST INDIES!
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
The batsman has nudged the ball fine down the leg side. Three runs added to the total. The stand moves to 21.
Full and outside off, watchfully defended by coming forward.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
SIX! Thump! Tossed up outside off, Brathwaite comes down the track and sends it soaring over long on! Moves to 33 from 33 balls.
On middle, Bravo goes back and works it towards backward square leg.
Short again, outside off, punched to sweeper cover for a single.
FOUR! Poor ball. Short and outside off, spinning away, Brathwaite rocks back and cuts it through the covers for a boundary. The stand is worth 11 now. 417 more needed for a win.
Outside off, punched through the covers for a couple.
Tossed up outside off, Brathwaite drives it straight to mid off.
A full toss on off, worked wide of long on for a single.
Full and outside off, blocked out watchfully.

Full on middle, worked down to long on for a single.
Full and outside off, pushed back to Babar.

On middle and leg, worked through mid-wicket for a run.
Full on middle, flicked past short leg for a single through mid-wicket. Moves to 20.
Flatter around off, Kraigg goes back and defends.
Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
Comes down the track but is yorked. Bunts it back to the bowler.
Landed around off, spinning away, Brathwaite goes back and punches it to cover.
The batsman works it down the leg side.

Full on middle, pushed to the off side.
The batsman flicks it away with a wristy shot.
On middle and off, pushed back to the bowler.
On middle and leg, played straight to short leg.
Tossed up on middle and leg, pushed down to long on for a single.
DARREN BRAVO comes in at number 3, replacing Johnson.

OUT! DRAGGED ON! Yasir strikes in his second over. Not the best of balls, landed outside leg, Johnson gets down to sweep but misses. The ball hits his pads, then his arm and hits the stumps. Johnson is down on his haunches, with his hands on his helmet. Bad luck for him. He should have put it away.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
A slight mix-up but safe. Johnson pushes it towards covers and sets off for a single, comes halfway for a single but is sent back.
Excellent running. Landed around middle, Brathwaite goes back and helps it through backward square leg for three excellently run runs. 428 more needed for a win now.
Tossed up around leg, swept through square leg for a single.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Full and around off this time, watchfully defended by coming forward.
Tossed up outside off, Brathwaite comes down the track and pushes it to short extra cover.
Full on middle and leg, worked past short leg for a single.
Shortish outside off, punched towards short extra cover.
Landed outside off, punched back to the bowler.
ZULFIQAR BABAR eventually comes on from the other end.
Short around off, spinning away, punched towards cover.
Comes down the track and blocks.

Full and outside off, pushed towards cover.
FOUR! Excellent use of the feet! Full on middle, Brathwaite comes down the track, gets to the pitch of the ball and works it between mid on and mid-wicket for a boundary!
Outside off, left alone.

Here comes the game changer. YASIR SHAH comes on to bowl in the 6th over of the innings. It was supposed to be Zulfiqar Babar initially but Misbah had a discussion with Younis and called Yasir instead.

Good discussion between Ian Bishop and Waqar Younis on air. Both observe that neither of Misbah nor Holder has had confidence in keeping three slips. But they are disappointed in not giving the fast bowlers a packed slip cordon, especially with the new ball.
A length ball on middle, whipped behind square leg for a couple.
On a good length on middle, defended back to the bowler.
That is a beautiful delivery. Sohail lands it on a length around off, then gets it to move away. Johnson pokes inside the line and is beaten.
Full and around off, angling in, worked with the angle through mid-wicket for a single. 439 more needed for a win now.
Full and outside off, pushed towards extra cover.

FOUR! Lovely shot. Landed slightly wider outside off, on a length between full and good, Brathwaite just punches it through the covers and the ball races away to the ropes. The cherry has not done anything so far. No swing, no movement, nothing. Brathwaite moves to 11.
Full and straight, defended back to the bowler.
FOUR! First boundary of the run chase. Short and wide outside off, Johnson goes after it and cuts it behind point for a boundary.
Fuller and outside off, pushed towards cover.

On a good length outside off, tapped through the covers for a single.
Fuller length ball outside off, not played at.
Down the leg side, Leon misses his flick and the ball goes off his thigh pads and rolls to the keeper.
Wide outside off, left alone.
On middle and leg, flicked away for a single.
Oohhh... loose shot. Landed outside off, Brathwaite pushes away from his body without moving his feet and gets a thick inside edge onto his pads. That could have so easily crashed into the stumps.
FOUR! Easy pickings. Half volley on middle, Brathwaite flicks it through mid-wicket and gets a boundary.
